new_packages.label: מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת וּקְלִפָּה
new_packages.reason: The source text explicitly equates foreign thoughts with קליפה and קומה שלמה. These three concepts form a bechina-connected cluster: each foreign thought IS a husk, and IS a complete form. This constitutes 3 bechina-connected concepts forming an independent thematic domain of evil forces encountered during prayer.

proposed_edges.proof: כִּי כָל מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה הוּא קְלִפָּה
כָל מַחֲשָׁבָה וּמַחֲשָׁבָה הִיא קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה

new_packages.mirror_notes: This evil package (foreign thoughts as husks) mirrors the good side of prayer (תפלה). The good mirror would be a package around תפלה/prayer-in-order, but the source text does not provide bechina identifications for the prayer side — only eitza (through prayer one defeats the husks).

observations: Torah #122 is a short teaching with a clear bechina core: foreign thoughts ARE husks/shells with a complete form. The teaching's practical dimension (praying in order defeats them) is eitza, not bechina. The war metaphor is illustrative, not an identity statement. One new evil-polarity package of 3 nodes is proposed, meeting the minimum threshold of 3 bechina-connected concepts.
